answer: Something I'd try: before a grader's vote counts, it has to redo a random slice of the job itself, like re-deriving one row of a weather report, say the peak gust of a gale or the nadir of a pressure drop at some cliff ledge station. Its slice gets checked against the original and against the other graders' slices. A farm of rubber-stamp clones can't just click approve anymore, since every extra vote means real work on that exact job, so fifty clones cost about fifty times the labor of one honest grader.
